chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakill (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Musa ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of his father, who linked it up to God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family):

Umm Salma asked him, 'May my father and mother be your ransom! If a woman has had two husbands who die and enter Heaven, which one will she belong to?' He said, 'O Umm Salma! She will choose the one who was best in character and best to his family. O Umm Salma! Good character will result in the best of this world and the Hereafter.'

key_terms.أُمَّ سَلَمَ: Umm Salma, a prominent companion of the Prophet
key_terms.الْآخِرَة: the Hereafter, the eternal life after death
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: to link up or elevate the chain of narration to a higher authority (the Prophet)

ai.seo_question: Which husband does a woman belong to in Heaven if she had two?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Umm al-Salma inquires about the marital status of a woman with two deceased husbands in the afterlife, to which the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) responds that she will choose the husband with the superior moral character (*husn al-khuluq*) and kindness to his family. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on ethical conduct as the decisive factor for spiritual merit, affirming that good character serves as a comprehensive key to success in both this world and the Hereafter.
